title: Console export connector playbook and tenant stratification for reporting requests
creator: Elena Morris
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit a mix of console/reporting requests (scheduled exports, ad-hoc slices, cost breakdowns, dashboard request) but the current intake lacks consistent connector guidance and tenant stratification. As a result high-value requests are delayed, duplicates created, and SRE/engineering scope creep occurs.

Goal: Define a playbook and decision matrix that routes reporting requests to the correct delivery path (self-serve export template, scheduled connector, product feature, or concierge engineering), and produce per-tenant stratification rules so that sales/CS and PMs can set SLAs, pricing triggers, and implementation expectations.

Scope:
- Intake form/fields and evidence required for different lanes (S3/BigQuery target, frequency, retention, row-level security needs, query complexity)
- Priority scoring rubric (business value, technical complexity, security/regulatory constraints, cost delta)
- Mapping from request archetype to delivery lane: self-serve, template + enablement, scheduled export (platform-run), console feature roadmap, or engineering project
- Connector playbook for S3, GCS, BigQuery, Snowflake including schema contracts, sample manifests, cost estimation metrics and expected telemetry
- Tenant stratification rules (by ARR, security classification, data sensitivity, request frequency) and contract triggers for dedicated onboarding and SLA
- Acceptance criteria, telemetry, and dashboard to triage and measure throughput and lead time

Deliverables:
- Intake form spec (fields + validation + evidence requirements)
- Playbook doc for connector types (runbook + checklist)
- Prioritization matrix and scoring spreadsheet
- Implementation plan for enabling 3 pilot tenants
- Dashboard to monitor intake funnel, lead times, and backlog distribution

Out-of-scope: Full engineering implementation of connectors; this ticket is for PM playbook, acceptance criteria, and pilot coordination.

Decision trade-offs:
- Strict evidence requirement vs. faster acceptance: we will enforce minimum evidence for tenant-stratified lanes to reduce rework (trade-off: higher friction up-front)
- Offer limited self-serve templates for common export shapes rather than unlimited custom exports to contain engineering cost

Stakeholders:
- CS: Priya Nair (escalation + customer scoping)
- Solutions Eng: Michael Alvarez (connector feasibility)
- Infra/Eng: Marcus Chen (assignee, engineering liaison)
- Security & Compliance: Hana Sato (approvals for regulated tenants)
- Sales: Jordan Smith (pricing triggers)

Metrics/KPIs:
- Median intake-to-delivery time by lane (target: self-serve < 3 days, scheduled export < 14 days, org feature > 30 days)
- Percentage of requests correctly routed (target > 90%)
- Number of duplicate requests prevented
- Post-delivery CS satisfaction score (target >= 4/5)

Acceptance criteria:
- Intake form prototype with validation in staging
- Playbook doc reviewed and approved by CS, SE, Security
- Prioritization matrix published and linked in ticketing system
- Pilot with 3 tenants (1 small, 1 mid, 1 enterprise) scheduled and scoped

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: finalize intake form and priority rubric
- Week 2–3: review with stakeholders, update playbook
- Week 4–6: run pilots and collect feedback
- Week 7: iterate and prepare handoff to triage/ops team

Risks:
- Underestimated connector implementation complexity leading to missed SLA
- Data privacy/regulatory blockers for some tenants
- Misclassification of tenant leading to wrong SLA expectations
